stem.text: Let \( f(x) = \frac{5 \left(x + 6\right)^{\frac{2}{3}}}{x + 3} \) for \( x \ne -3 \), where \( \left(x + 6\right)^{\frac{2}{3}} \) is the square of the real cube root. Find all critical points of f.

answer_key.label: The critical points of f are x = -12 and x = -6.

worked_solution.text: For x other than -6 and -3, the quotient and chain rules give \( f'(x) = \frac{- 5 x - 60}{3 \left(x + 3\right)^{2} \sqrt[3]{x + 6}} \).
Setting \( f'(x) = 0 \) gives x = -12, and f is defined there, so x = -12 is a critical point.
worked_solution.rule_named: critical point where the derivative is zero

worked_solution.text: At x = -6 the function is defined, \( f(-6) = 0 \), and the factor in the denominator is 0 while the numerator is not, so the graph of f has a cusp there; so the derivative fails to exist at an input in the domain and x = -6 is a critical point. At x = -3 the derivative also fails to exist, but f is not defined there, so x = -3 is not a critical point.
worked_solution.rule_named: critical point where the derivative fails to exist

options.label: The critical points of f are x = -12, x = -6 and x = -3.
options.derivation: the excluded input -3, where f' fails to exist but f is undefined, kept as a critical point

The critical points of f are x = -12 and x = -3.
options.derivation: the excluded input -3 taken as the place where f' fails to exist, and the cusp or tangent at -6 missed
